takeaways: OpenID Connect adds an ID token on top of OAuth 2.0 so apps learn who you are, while the access token still governs what they may do.
Microsoft Entra ID speaks OpenID Connect, which is why one morning sign-in carries you into Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive and third-party apps.
Apps must validate every ID token and must never treat it as a permission, and server-to-server scenarios need the OAuth client credentials flow instead.
hook: Every Sign in with Microsoft button relies on a standard most people never notice. This episode explains OpenID Connect for Microsoft 365 users, makers and admins: how the sign-in flow works, what sits inside an ID token and how it relates to OAuth 2.0, SAML and Entra ID. You also learn the common mistakes that turn a strong standard into a weak door.
